headline.text: Free Gemini gets one model

body.text: Google's support page says that from Oct. 9, Gemini app users without a paid plan lose Flash and Pro. Today they pick a model from a menu. After the change, every free request uses Flash-Lite.

headline.text: The cheapest paid plan loses Pro too

body.text: Google says AI Plus subscribers will keep Flash-Lite and Flash but lose Pro, which its support page calls its most advanced model, for complex math and coding. An email will give them the date.

headline.text: Keeping Pro means moving up a tier

body.text: Pro will require AI Pro or AI Ultra. Yahoo Creators calculates that a Plus subscriber who wants to keep Pro would pay roughly $15 more a month, or $180 a year, at current prices.

headline.text: Some U.S. college students can get Pro free for a year

body.text: Yahoo Creators says eligible U.S. college students can redeem a free year of AI Pro through Dec. 31, 2026. It needs a valid payment method and charges $19.99 a month afterward unless canceled.

headline.text: New effort levels come with a catch

body.text: Google is adding low, medium and high effort levels for each available model. 9to5Google says they look to be coming in October; PCMag says soon.

slides.quote_excerpt: …provide more thorough answers to queries, but will also use more of your limit.

headline.text: The second plan overhaul this year

body.text: 9to5Google says the limits follow a compute-based usage change Google made in May. PCMag suggests rising storage and component costs, potentially. Google has not stated a reason in these reports.

headline.text: What is still unclear

body.text: Plus subscribers' exact date is coming by email, and Yahoo Creators says it may differ from Oct. 9. On Deep Think, 9to5Google says AI Pro gets it; Engadget says AI Ultra subscribers do.

caption.text:
Google says that from Oct. 9, Gemini app users without a paid Google AI plan will lose access to the Flash and Pro models and be limited to Flash-Lite. The change comes from an updated Google support page, reported by 9to5Google, PCMag and Engadget.

Google AI Plus subscribers ($4.99 a month in the US) will also lose Pro, on a date Google says it will explain by email. Yahoo Creators says that date may differ from Oct. 9. Pro will require AI Pro ($19.99 a month) or AI Ultra. Google describes Pro as its most advanced model, for complex math and coding, and Flash-Lite as built for speed and everyday tasks like summarizing and brainstorming. PCMag says this is the second overhaul of Google's AI plans this year and suggests rising costs may be a factor. Google has not given a reason in these reports.

Would you pay $19.99 a month to keep Pro?

Follow Helios Group for plain-English updates on AI changes that hit the tools you already use.

Source: 9to5Google, Oct. 3, 2026; PCMag, Oct. 5, 2026; Engadget, Oct. 6, 2026; Yahoo Creators, Oct. 6, 2026.

edit_notes: Cover leads with Google (well_known true); 'says' keeps the claim attribution to the support page.
Skipped single-source quotes Q1 and Q3; paraphrased the email detail instead.
Quote slide uses an exact excerpt of Q2 to stay under 140 chars.
Deep Think disagreement shown on the closing slide with both sources named rather than picking one.
Left out the 2x/4x/5x usage multiples because sources disagree and the page may be cached.
Left out Gemini 4 Argon, 1 billion users and the Menlo survey as off the main event.
Yahoo's $15/$180 figure attributed to Yahoo Creators since it is the writer's calculation.
Why-now slide combines B1 with PCMag's hedged cost suggestion and notes Google gave no reason.
Student offer slide kept because it is a practical consequence for readers who rely on Pro for studying; single-source attribution to Yahoo Creators.
Cover chosen 1: states who did what and the date directly.
Slide 7 cites only B1 and F10 for the one-clause context; no earlier events beyond that.
